evidence.title: Microeconomics course-area controls
evidence.alt: Faculty Build Composer with Microeconomics selected in the course-area menu and Micro starter combinations displayed.
evidence.caption: Microeconomics is selected, so the Composer displays only Micro starter combinations and concept inventory.

evidence.title: Macroeconomics concept selection
evidence.alt: Macroeconomics Composer inventory with Aggregate Demand selected and burgundy discipline accents on Macro concept cards.
evidence.caption: Aggregate Demand is selected while the Macro inventory retains its discipline-specific accent and related-concept controls.

evidence.title: Ten-mode selection
evidence.alt: Mode-selection screen showing Standard Campaign, Timed Trial, Exam Drill, Quiz, Unlimited Practice, Legendary Mode, Score Attack, Trial by Graph, Fading Fortune, and Risk and Reward.
evidence.caption: The current generated game supports ten modes; only faculty-enabled modes appear for students.

evidence.title: Quiz question-count selector
evidence.alt: Quiz setup dialog with a student-selectable question count from 1 through 15 and instructor-selected concepts kept fixed.
evidence.caption: Quiz lets students choose 1-15 questions without changing the instructor-selected concepts.

evidence.title: Trial by Graph
evidence.alt: Trial by Graph question showing readable marginal cost, average total cost, and average variable cost curves with standard answer controls.
evidence.caption: Every Trial by Graph item requires the audited graph shown with the question.

evidence.title: Fading Fortune
evidence.alt: Fading Fortune question after two wrong answer choices have disappeared, leaving two choices and a current value of 50 points.
evidence.caption: Two faded choices reduce the available question value from 100 to 50 points.

evidence.title: Risk and Reward
evidence.alt: Risk and Reward wager screen with a 1,000-point bankroll and choices to risk 10%, 25%, 50%, or all in before seeing the question.
evidence.caption: Students lock a wager before the question and answers are revealed.

evidence.title: Conceptual application
evidence.alt: Conceptual application question asking the student to apply an economic idea in a current game screen.
evidence.caption: Conceptual items ask students to interpret and apply, not only recall.

evidence.title: Economic calculation
evidence.alt: Calculation question asking the student to compute a four-firm concentration ratio from five market shares.
evidence.caption: The item requires a four-firm concentration-ratio calculation from market-share data.

evidence.title: Checkpoint evidence
evidence.alt: Checkpoint encounter using a short scaffold of higher-difficulty questions tied to one eligible learning objective.
evidence.caption: Campaign checkpoints build a short mastery scaffold around an eligible learning objective.

evidence.title: Mastery Report 2.0 recommendation
evidence.alt: Mastery Report showing Scarcity as the weakest concept, a button to open its Concept Review, and a next move to practice Application questions.
evidence.caption: Weak Scarcity evidence and Application-question trouble resolve to GEN-ECON-01 and a targeted next move.

evidence.title: Scarcity Concept Review
evidence.alt: GEN-ECON-01 Scarcity Concept Review with Core Idea, How to Recognize It, Watch Out, Worked Example, and Check Yourself sections; no graph is present.
evidence.caption: The non-graph sample repairs the relationship among limited resources, choices, and tradeoffs.

evidence.title: Price Elasticity of Demand Concept Review
evidence.alt: MICRO-04 Price Elasticity of Demand Concept Review with recognition cues, a common mistake, a midpoint-elasticity worked example, a labeled demand graph, and a check-yourself prompt.
evidence.caption: The graph-based sample pairs the midpoint calculation with a labeled demand curve and interpretation.
